Nephrology

Comprehensive Nephrology Services

Our Commitment to Kidney Health and Wellness at Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital

At Sri Lakshmi Specialty Hospital, we offer a wide range of nephrology services to address the diverse needs of individuals with kidney-related conditions. Whether you are dealing with kidney disease, hypertension, or other renal disorders, our team is here to provide expert diagnosis, innovative treatments, and personalized care to help you achieve and maintain optimal kidney health.

Key Nephrology Services Include:
Nephrology Consultations:

Comprehensive evaluations by experienced nephrologists to diagnose and manage a variety of kidney-related conditions, including chronic kidney disease (CKD), acute kidney injury (AKI), glomerulonephritis, and electrolyte disorders.

Dialysis Services:

Comprehensive dialysis services, including hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis, for patients with advanced kidney failure or end-stage renal disease (ESRD), performed in our state-of-the-art dialysis center by skilled nephrology nurses and technicians.

Kidney Transplantation:

Evaluation, preparation, and post-transplant care for patients undergoing kidney transplantation, including pre-transplant assessments, donor compatibility testing, and long-term transplant management.

Hypertension Management:

Specialized care for patients with hypertension (high blood pressure) and its associated complications, including renal hypertension, with a focus on blood pressure control and kidney protection.

Electrolyte and Acid-Base Disorders:

 Diagnosis and treatment of electrolyte imbalances, such as hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, and metabolic acidosis, to restore normal kidney function and prevent complications.

Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) Management:

Comprehensive management of CKD at all stages, including lifestyle modifications, medication therapy, and nutritional counseling, to slow disease progression and improve quality of life

Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) Care:

 Rapid diagnosis and treatment of AKI, including supportive measures and renal replacement therapy (dialysis), to prevent further kidney damage and promote recovery.

Pediatric Nephrology:

Specialized care for children with kidney-related conditions, including congenital anomalies, urinary tract infections, nephrotic syndrome, and hereditary kidney disorders, to ensure optimal kidney health and growth.

Specialized Kidney Cares

Expertise Across a Range of Kidney Conditions at Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital

Sri Lakshmi Specialty Hospital is home to a team of highly skilled nephrologists with expertise in diagnosing and treating a wide range of kidney-related conditions. Whether you are dealing with a common kidney disorder or a complex renal issue, our specialists are here to provide expert care and personalized treatment options to meet your unique needs.

Key Kidney Specialties Include:
Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD):

Comprehensive evaluation and management of CKD at all stages, including conservative measures, medication therapy, and renal replacement therapy (dialysis or transplant) for advanced disease.

Acute Kidney Injury (AKI):

Rapid diagnosis and treatment of AKI, including identification and correction of underlying causes, supportive care, and renal replacement therapy (dialysis) when necessary, to prevent further kidney damage and promote recovery.

Glomerular Disorders:

Evaluation and management of glomerular diseases, including glomerulonephritis, lupus nephritis, IgA nephropathy, and membranous nephropathy, with a focus on disease-specific therapies and renal protection strategies.

Polycystic Kidney Disease (PKD):

Specialized care for patients with PKD, including surveillance imaging, blood pressure management, and treatment of complications such as cyst infection, kidney stones, and hypertension.

Specialized care for patients with PKD, including surveillance imaging, blood pressure management, and treatment of complications such as cyst infection, kidney stones, and hypertension.

Diabetic Kidney Disease:

 Comprehensive management of diabetic nephropathy, including glycemic control, blood pressure management, and renoprotective therapies, to slow the progression of kidney damage and reduce the risk of complications.

Hypertensive Kidney Disease:

Targeted treatment of hypertensive nephropathy, including blood pressure control, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) blockade, and lifestyle modifications, to preserve kidney function and prevent cardiovascular complications.

Kidney Stone Disease:

Evaluation and management of kidney stones, including medical therapy, dietary modifications, and minimally invasive procedures (such as lithotripsy or ureteroscopy) for stone removal and prevention of recurrence

Hereditary Kidney Disorders:

Genetic counseling, screening, and management of hereditary kidney diseases, including autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), Alport syndrome, and Fabry disease, to optimize renal health and genetic counseling for at-risk individuals and families.

What function do the kidneys provide in the body?

In order to create urine, the kidneys filter waste materials and extra fluid from the blood. They also assist in controlling blood pressure and electrolyte levels.

What signs and symptoms of renal illness are typical?

Fatigue, edema, changes in urine output or appearance, chronic itching, nausea, and appetite changes are some of the common signs of kidney disease.

Kidney disease: is it preventable?

By controlling underlying illnesses including diabetes and hypertension, leading a healthy lifestyle, and limiting the use of over-the-counter painkillers, kidney disease can occasionally be avoided or postponed.

How frequently should my kidney function be evaluated?

Regular renal function testing is recommended for people who have conditions like diabetes or hypertension that increase their risk of kidney disease. Based on your health situation, your doctor can decide on the right frequency.

Is renal illness curable?

The fundamental reason affects whether kidney illness may be cured. While certain forms of kidney illness can be managed or cured, others may develop to the point where they are irreversible and call for dialysis or transplantation.

How long does it take to recover from a kidney transplant?

Individuals with kidney transplants recover at different rates. Patients typically require a few days to a week in the hospital, as well as several weeks of recuperation and follow-up care.

Can someone with renal illness lead a normal life?

Many people with renal illness can enjoy happy lives with the right care and lifestyle changes. The course of treatment, however, will be determined by the kidney disease's stage and severity.

How can we help you?
What does a urologist do?

A urologist is a medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of conditions affecting the urinary tract and male reproductive system. They manage conditions such as kidney stones, urinary tract infections, prostate issues, and urological cancers.

When should I see a urologist?

You should consider seeing a urologist if you experience symptoms such as frequent urination, painful urination, blood in urine, kidney stones, erectile dysfunction, or concerns about male fertility.

How can I prevent kidney stones?

To reduce the risk of kidney stones, drink plenty of water, maintain a balanced diet, limit salt intake, and avoid excessive consumption of foods high in oxalate (e.g., spinach, nuts).

Are urinary tract infections (UTIs) more common in women?

Yes, UTIs are more common in women due to their shorter urethra, which allows bacteria to reach the bladder more easily. However, UTIs can occur in men as well.

Is prostate cancer curable?

Prostate cancer is often treatable, especially when detected early. Treatment options may include surgery, radiation therapy, hormone therapy, and active surveillance for low-risk cases.

What is the recovery time after urological surgery?

Recovery time varies depending on the type of surgery and the individual's health. Minimally invasive procedures typically have shorter recovery times than open surgeries.

Can urological conditions affect sexual health?

Yes, certain urological conditions, such as erectile dysfunction, Peyronie's disease, and prostate issues, can affect sexual health and function.

How can we help you?
What is diabetes?

Diabetes is a chronic condition in which the body has difficulty regulating blood sugar (glucose). There are two main types: type 1 diabetes, which is an autoimmune condition where the body's immune system attacks the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas, and type 2 diabetes, which occurs when the body becomes resistant to insulin or does not produce enough insulin.

What are the symptoms of diabetes?

Common symptoms of diabetes include frequent urination, excessive thirst, unexplained weight loss, increased hunger, fatigue, and slow wound healing. However, some people with type 2 diabetes may have mild or no symptoms, leading to undiagnosed diabetes.

Can diabetes be prevented?

Type 1 diabetes cannot be prevented as it is an autoimmune condition. However, type 2 diabetes can often be prevented or delayed through lifestyle modifications such as healthy eating, regular exercise, and maintaining a healthy weight.

How often should I check my blood sugar levels?

The frequency of blood sugar monitoring depends on the type of diabetes, the treatment plan, and the healthcare provider's recommendations. Some patients may need to monitor several times a day, while others may require less frequent monitoring.

Can diabetes be cured?

As of now, there is no cure for diabetes. However, with proper management and lifestyle changes, many people with diabetes can lead healthy and fulfilling lives.

Is it safe for women with diabetes to get pregnant?

With careful planning and proper medical Supervision, women with diabetes can have healthy pregnancies. Pre-pregnancy counseling and close monitoring during pregnancy are crucial to ensure optimal outcomes for both the mother and the baby.

Can I still eat my favorite foods if I have diabetes?

Yes, you can enjoy your favorite foods in moderation. A balanced diet that includes a variety of foods and portion control is key to managing blood sugar levels.

How can I prevent complications from diabetes?

To prevent complications, it's essential to keep blood sugar levels under control, attend regular medical check-ups, follow your healthcare provider's recommendations, and adopt a healthy lifestyle.

How can we help you?
When should I call for emergency medical assistance?

Call for emergency medical assistance immediately if you encounter a life-threatening situation, such as:

-        Chest pain or suspected heart attack

-        Difficulty breathing or sudden shortness of breath

-        Unconsciousness or altered mental status

-        Severe bleeding that cannot be controlled

-        Suspected stroke (sudden numbness, weakness, or slurred speech)

-        Choking or difficulty swallowing

-        Seizures or convulsions

-        Severe allergic reactions with difficulty breathing or swelling of the face and throat

What should I do if someone around me experiences a sudden cardiac arrest?

If someone experiences a sudden cardiac arrest, immediately call for emergency medical assistance and start performing hands-only CPR until help arrives.

Is emergency care provided on a first-come, first-served basis?

No, emergency care is provided based on the severity of the patient's condition. Triage is performed to prioritize patients with life-threatening conditions to receive immediate attention.

What information should I provide to emergency responders when I call for help?

When calling for emergency medical assistance, be prepared to provide the following information:

-        Your name and location (address or landmarks)

-        The nature of the medical emergency or injury

-        The number of patients involved and their condition

-        Any specific medical conditions or known allergies of the patient

Can I visit the emergency room for non-emergency conditions?

Emergency rooms are designed to handle life-threatening and urgent medical conditions. For non-life-threatening conditions or minor injuries, it is best to visit an urgent care center or your primary care physician.

How can we help you?
What are the common risk factors for heart disease?

Common risk factors for heart disease include high blood pressure, high cholesterol levels, smoking, obesity, physical inactivity, diabetes, a family history of heart disease, and an unhealthy diet.

How often should I have my cholesterol levels checked?

The frequency of cholesterol checks depends on your age, risk factors, and overall health. Generally, adults should have their cholesterol levels checked at least every five years. If you have specific risk factors, more frequent testing may be necessary.

Can heart disease be prevented?

Yes, many cases of heart disease can be prevented or delayed through lifestyle modifications such as a healthy diet, regular exercise, not smoking, and managing other risk factors like high blood pressure and diabetes.

What are the warning signs of a heart attack?

Warning signs of a heart attack may include chest pain or discomfort, shortness of breath, pain or discomfort in the arms, back, neck, jaw, or stomach, and nausea or lightheadedness. It's essential to seek immediate medical attention if you experience these symptoms.

How can I reduce my risk of developing heart disease?

You can reduce your risk of heart disease by adopting a heart-healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise, maintaining a healthy weight, eating a balanced diet, not smoking, managing stress, and following your doctor's recommendations for managing any existing medical conditions.

What should I do if I have a family history of heart disease?

If you have a family history of heart disease, it's essential to inform your doctor. They can assess your individual risk and recommend appropriate preventive measures and screenings.

Can heart disease affect women differently than men?

Yes, heart disease can present differently in women than in men. Women may experience atypical symptoms during a heart attack, such as shortness of breath, nausea, and back or jaw pain. It's essential for women to be aware of these differences and seek medical attention if they experience any concerning symptoms.

How long does it take to recover from heart surgery?

Recovery time varies depending on the type of heart surgery, the patient's overall health, and the complexity of the procedure. Generally, patients may need several weeks to a few months to fully recover and resume normal activities.

How can we help you?
How often should I have a Pap smear?

Pap smears are typically recommended every three years for women aged 21 to 29 with normal results. For women aged 30 to 65, a combination of Pap smears and human papillomavirus (HPV) testing is recommended every five years.

What are the common symptoms of gynecological conditions?

Common symptoms of gynecological conditions include abnormal vaginal bleeding, pelvic pain, pain during intercourse, unusual vaginal discharge, itching, and changes in menstrual patterns. If you experience any concerning symptoms, it's essential to seek medical advice promptly.

Is it normal to have irregular periods?

In some cases, irregular periods can be normal, especially during adolescence and perimenopause. However, irregular periods can also indicate underlying gynecological issues like hormonal imbalances, PCOS, or thyroid disorders. If you are concerned about your menstrual patterns, consult with a gynecologist

When should I schedule my first prenatal visit?

It is recommended to schedule your first prenatal visit as soon as you know you are pregnant or if you suspect you might be pregnant. Early prenatal care is essential for monitoring the pregnancy from its earliest stages and establishing a healthy foundation for both mother and baby.

What can I expect during a prenatal visit?

During a prenatal visit, your obstetrician will conduct a physical examination, review your medical history, perform ultrasound scans to assess the baby's development, and discuss any concerns or questions you may have about your pregnancy.

How often should I have prenatal check-ups?

The frequency of prenatal check-ups may vary depending on your specific medical needs and the stage of your pregnancy. In general, regular prenatal visits are scheduled approximately once a month during the first two trimesters and then more frequently as the due date approaches.

FAQs

How does it differ from traditional surgery?

Laparoscopic surgery, also known as minimally invasive surgery or keyhole surgery, involves making small incisions in the abdomen through which a tiny camera and specialized surgical instruments are inserted. This approach allows surgeons to perform complex procedures with smaller incisions compared to traditional open surgery. The benefits of laparoscopic surgery include reduced postoperative pain, quicker recovery times, smaller scars, shorter hospital stays, and lower risk of infection.

How long does it take to recover from laparoscopic surgery?

Recovery time after laparoscopic surgery varies depending on the type of procedure and individual factors. In general, most patients can resume their normal activities within a few days to a week after surgery. However, the surgeon will provide specific postoperative care instructions to optimize your recovery.

What conditions can be treated through laparoscopic surgery?

Laparoscopic surgery can be used to treat various conditions, including gallbladder diseases (gallstones, cholecystitis), hernias (inguinal, umbilical, incisional), gastrointestinal disorders (ulcers, diverticulitis), and certain cancers (colon, stomach, pancreas). It is also utilized for procedures like laparoscopic appendectomy, anti-reflux surgery, and ovarian cystectomy.

How do I prepare for surgery?

Your surgeon will provide detailed preoperative instructions to help you prepare for the procedure. These may include fasting instructions, stopping certain medications, and arranging for someone to drive you home after the surgery. It's crucial to follow these guidelines to ensure a safe and successful surgery.

What are the potential risks of surgery?

Like any surgical procedure, laparoscopic surgery carries some risks. These risks can include bleeding, infection, damage to surrounding organs, and adverse reactions to anesthesia. However, our experienced surgical team takes all necessary precautions to minimize these risks and ensure the best possible outcome.

Will I have scars after laparoscopic surgery?

While laparoscopic surgery involves small incisions, there will still be some scars. However, these scars are typically much smaller and less noticeable than those from traditional open surgery. Over time, the scars tend to fade and become less visible.

Is laparoscopic surgery suitable for everyone?

Laparoscopic surgery may not be suitable for every patient or condition. Factors such as the patient's overall health, the complexity of the procedure, and previous abdominal surgeries may influence the decision to opt for laparoscopic surgery. Your surgeon will discuss the most appropriate treatment option based on your individual case.

Will I need to stay in the hospital after surgery?

The length of hospital stay depends on the specific procedure and your individual recovery progress. Many laparoscopic surgeries are performed on an outpatient basis, allowing patients to go home the same day. However, some procedures may require an overnight stay for monitoring.

How can we help you?
What does a neurologist do?

A neurologist is a medical doctor who specializes in diagnosing and treating diseases and disorders of the nervous system. They manage conditions such as epilepsy, stroke, Superple sclerosis, movement disorders, and peripheral nerve disorders.

What are common symptoms of neurological disorders?

Common symptoms of neurological disorders may include headaches, seizures, weakness, numbness, difficulty walking, tremors, memory problems, and changes in speech or vision.

What causes neurological disorders?

Neurological disorders can have various causes, including genetics, infections, immune system disorders, trauma, tumors, and degenerative conditions.

When should I see a neurologist?

You should consider seeing a neurologist if you experience persistent or concerning neurological symptoms, such as unexplained headaches, seizures, weakness, balance problems, or changes in cognition.

Can neurological conditions be cured?

The outcome and treatment options depend on the specific neurological condition. While some conditions can be managed effectively and symptoms improved, others may require ongoing treatment and symptom management.

What is a stroke, and how is it treated?

A stroke occurs when blood flow to the brain is interrupted, leading to brain cell damage. Treatment for stroke includes time-sensitive interventions such as clot-dissolving medications (thrombolytics) and, in some cases, mechanical thrombectomy to remove the clot.

Can neurology treatment be combined with other medical specialties?

Yes, neurology often collaborates with other medical specialties, such as neurosurgery, physical medicine and rehabilitation, and psychiatry, to provide comprehensive care for patients with complex neurological conditions.

Are there ways to prevent neurological disorders?

While not all neurological disorders can be prevented, adopting a healthy lifestyle, managing chronic conditions (e.g., diabetes, hypertension), wearing helmets during activities with head injury risks, and avoiding toxins or infections that can affect the nervous system may reduce the risk of some conditions.

About Us

Nurturing Health, Empowering Lives

Who We Are

Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital, KR Puram: Leading Healthcare Excellence

Welcome to Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital in KR Puram, Bangalore! Founded in 2002 by Dr. Sambashiva, our hospital is part of the renowned Sri Lakshmi Group of Hospitals. We are dedicated to making top-quality healthcare affordable and accessible to everyone in the KR Puram area.

Our 50-bed facility is equipped with the latest medical technologies and staffed by a team of expert doctors. We offer a wide range of specialized services, including: Heart Care, Emergency and Trauma Care, Kidney Care, Brain and Nerve Care, Men’s Health, General and Keyhole Surgery, Women’s Health

At Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital, our goal is to provide the best possible care in a comfortable and compassionate environment. Whether you need a routine check-up or advanced medical treatment, our experienced specialists are here to help.

Come experience the difference at Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital, where we are committed to your health and well-being!

Discover more
Our Value

Upholding Excellence, Empathy, and Integrity in Every Patient Journey

Our Vision

At Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital, KR Puram, our vision is to transform healthcare by making it affordable and within reach for everyone. We are dedicated to bringing the latest medical technologies and top-notch facilities to our community, ensuring that every person receives the best care possible.

Our Mission

Our mission is to make advanced healthcare services and technology accessible and affordable for all. We believe that everyone deserves excellent medical care, which is why we have a team of the most experienced and caring doctors ready to serve you. At Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital, we are committed to improving the health and well-being of our community, one patient at a time.

Founder's Message

Greetings,

My journey in healthcare began with a simple belief: that everyone deserves access to quality medical care, regardless of their circumstances. Having witnessed the gaps in facilities and technology firsthand during my early days at a government hospital, I was inspired to make a difference.

In 2002, Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital was born out of this vision—to bring advanced healthcare closer to home in KR Puram. Beyond treatment, our mission extends to supporting our community. We’ve helped countless families with minimal medical bills and conducted outreach programs across Karnataka to promote health awareness.

Thank you for being a part of our journey. Together, let’s continue to provide compassionate care and make a positive impact on lives.

Warm regards,

Dr. Sambashiva

Founder, Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital

Why Choose Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital, KR Puram?

At Sri Lakshmi Super Speciality Hospital, your health and happiness are our top priorities. Choose us for quality care you can trust.

Trusted Experience

With over 25 years of caring for patients, our expert doctors provide the best possible medical care with skill and compassion.

Cutting-Edge Technology

Our hospital is equipped with the latest medical technology and modern facilities, ensuring you receive accurate diagnoses and effective treatments.

Affordable and Accessible Care

We believe everyone deserves excellent healthcare. That’s why we make our services both affordable and easily accessible to all.

Convenient Cashless Options

We offer cashless treatment through various private and government insurance schemes, making your experience hassle-free and convenient.

Comprehensive and Compassionate Care

From heart care to plastic surgery, our wide range of services is delivered with a personal touch. We focus on your unique needs to ensure you feel cared for every step of the way.
